title: Recover and exit without the failed provider dependency
description: Inject a dependency failure, choose a break-glass design, and pair it with an exit package. The model checks emergency authority, restore time, evidence, and target portability.
modelNote: Restore and exit times are illustrative planning estimates. Teams must measure them with workload-sized rehearsals.

scenarios.label: Provider identity unavailable
scenarios.detail: Normal administrators cannot authenticate to the provider account or control plane.

scenarios.label: Provider key and control planes isolated
scenarios.detail: The data plane exists, but provider key release and administrative APIs cannot be reached.

scenarios.label: Primary sovereign zone lost
scenarios.detail: A destructive regional incident requires restoration into clean capacity from isolated backups.

scenarios.label: Provider service must be exited
scenarios.detail: Policy or contract requires the workload to operate on an alternate platform within seven days.

recoveryPlans.label: Provider console break glass
recoveryPlans.detail: A root account and provider support workflow unlock the normal environment.

recoveryPlans.label: Local dual-control recovery
recoveryPlans.detail: Two local custodians activate escrowed credentials and keys from an offline runbook.

recoveryPlans.label: Independent recovery cell
recoveryPlans.detail: Local custodians restore into isolated clean capacity with independent identity, keys, backups, and evidence storage.

exitPackages.label: Provider-native backups only
exitPackages.detail: Backups exist, but schemas, identities, keys, service configuration, and a target are not independently prepared.

exitPackages.label: Versioned portable bundle
exitPackages.detail: Open data, schemas, infrastructure definitions, identity mappings, and key-transition procedures are exported and verified.

exitPackages.label: Rehearsed alternate platform
exitPackages.detail: The portable bundle is restored regularly on a replacement target with dependency substitutions and timed acceptance tests.
